turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have about twenty minutes, Hale, and a client call after that. Owen found out about a zero from his phone, in the middle of class. Who decided that, and why did nobody call me first?
The checker said 94 percent. That's the end of it.
"That's the end of it." Is it? Ninety-four percent is a machine's guess, and the company that sells it says not to use it as the sole basis for punishing a student. So what else do you have, Hale?
I don't need more proof than that.

"I don't need more proof than that." Your own procedure says otherwise: 4.3, software alone doesn't establish a concern. And 4.2 says you call me before any mark goes in, so I'm asking again, Hale, did anyone speak to Owen before that zero?
The software doesn't lie, unlike some people.
"Unlike some people." Say who you mean, Hale, because my child never lies, and I'm writing down that you said it. Are you calling Owen a liar, or me?

"Zero stands." Then that's one sentence I'll be repeating to the principal, along with the score, the "unlike some people," and the fact that nobody called me. Last chance, Hale: what do you have besides the software?
